chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Sa'id al-Adami, from Bishr ibn Bashshar al-Naysaburi, who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) informing him that the people before us differed regarding Divine Unity; some of them say He is a body, and others say He is an image. So he (peace be upon him) wrote back: 'Glory be to Him who has no limit, and cannot be described, and with whom nothing resembles! Nothing whatsoever is like unto Him. And He is the All-Hearing and the All-Seeing.'

key_terms.سُبْحَانَ مَنْ لَا يُحَدُّ: Glory to Him who has no limit

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia theological understanding of God's attributes regarding body and form?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* highlights the Mu'tazili-influenced Shia emphasis on divine transcendence (tanzih) by refuting anthropomorphic conceptions of God as either a body (jism) or a form (surah). Imam al-Rida (AS) succinctly encapsulates this by affirming that God is beyond spatial limits, human description, and similarity to creation, directly linking these attributes to the Quranic declaration of absolute uniqueness.
